text: M is a finite, nonempty, ordered set of nonidentity Hermitian n-qubit Pauli observables; signed representatives are retained for expectation values and separate phase-free symplectic vectors are retained for graph calculations.
rho is a positive semidefinite n-qubit operator with trace one.
Every inclusion-minimal Pauli product relation in M contains an anticommuting pair, so no such relation lies wholly inside a commuting context.
G_M is perfect: every induced subgraph H of G_M satisfies chi(H) = omega(H).
The sign-relaxed reduced stabilizer polytope keeps every deterministic sign assignment on each maximal commuting context and therefore outer-approximates the exact reduced stabilizer polytope.
M has no Pauli-active dependencies if and only if B_S equals the set of all sign assignments on S for every commuting context S.

The exact reduced stabilizer polytope equals the sign-relaxed polytope if and only if M has no Pauli-active dependencies; under that condition the exact and relaxed reduced robustness coincide for every state.

The sign-relaxed vertices affinely span R^m: for each coordinate i, extend P_i to a maximal commuting context and flip only its sign, producing a vertex difference 2e_i. Hence the relaxed primal is feasible for every b, and its objective is bounded below by 1 because ||x||_1 >= |sum x|.

By finite-dimensional strong linear-program duality, the relaxed robustness equals the maximum of b^T y + mu subject to |v_(S,f)^T y + mu| <= 1 for every maximal commuting context S and every unrestricted sign assignment f.
The dual feasible region of the sign-relaxed reduced robustness is alpha_|y|(G_M) + |mu| <= 1, so one maximum-weight independent-set computation separates a candidate dual point.
When M has no Pauli-active dependencies, the exact reduced robustness equals max b^T y + mu under alpha_|y|(G_M) + |mu| <= 1.
For a finite perfect graph G, the nonnegative vectors z satisfying alpha_z(G) <= 1 form the convex hull of clique incidence vectors, with the empty clique included.
If M has no Pauli-active dependencies and G_M is perfect, then for every n-qubit density operator rho, RoM_M(rho) = max(1, max over cliques Q of G_M of sum_(P in Q) |tr(P rho)|).

quantifiers: for every n-qubit density operator rho
logical_form.conclusion: closed-form equality only; the upper bound and attainment are separate claims

text: Under the same assumptions, RoM_M(rho) <= sqrt(omega(G_M)).
For a maximum clique Q, any state supported on the +1 eigenspace of |Q|^(-1/2) sum_(P in Q) P attains sqrt(omega(G_M)); hence the witness capacity equals that value.
Clifford conjugation rotates the signed Pauli measurement window while preserving commutation, product relations, solvability, and witness capacity.
For the reported eight-qubit samples, additional random Clifford rotations increase empirical detection coverage, most visibly for the Jordan-Wigner and Majorana-tree measurement sets.
For the one-qubit measurement set {X,Y,Z}, the independent finite-instance calculation agrees with the closed form and reaches sqrt(3) on the equal-axis +1 eigenstate.
For the two-qubit set {X1,X2,Z1Z2}, the independent finite-instance calculation agrees with the closed form and reaches sqrt(2) on a state supported in the +1 eigenspace of (X1+Z1Z2)/sqrt(2).

For the commuting set {X1X2,Z1Z2,Y1Y2}, the parity relation XX*ZZ*YY = -I leaves four exact sign vertices but the sign relaxation has eight; the nonphysical pseudo-vector (1,1,1) has exact signed-affine l1 value 2 and relaxed value 1.

For M={XX,ZZ,YY,IX,XI}, the frustration graph is the perfect graph C4 disjoint-union K1 but XX*ZZ*YY=-I is Pauli-active. For psi=(|00>+|01>+(1+i)|10>)/2, the graph-only clique formula is 1 while exact projected stabilizer primal and dual certificates both give RoM_M=5/4.
